name: Constrictive Pericarditis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Criteria for Constrictive Pericarditis

criteria.description: Evidence of pericardial thickening or calcification on imaging
Demonstration of ventricular interdependence on echocardiography or cardiac catheterization
Signs of right heart failure such as elevated jugular venous pressure and peripheral edema
Pericardial calcification on chest X-ray or CT scan
Hepatomegaly or ascites due to systemic venous congestion

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pericardial thickening or calcification plus clinical signs of right heart failure and evidence of ventricular interdependence on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires integration of clinical, imaging, and hemodynamic data.

pathognomonic.notes: Increase in jugular venous pressure on inspiration
Early diastolic sound due to abrupt cessation of ventricular filling

laboratory: Elevated liver function tests due to hepatic congestion
Mild elevation of inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
imaging: Pericardial thickening or calcification on CT or MRI
Septal bounce and ventricular interdependence on echocardiography
other: Hemodynamic findings on cardiac catheterization showing equalization of diastolic pressures

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of pericardial thickening or calcification
Etiology related to pulmonary hypertension or tricuspid valve disease

redFlags: Rapid progression of right heart failure symptoms
references: Maisch B, Seferović PM, Ristić AD, et al. Guidelines on the diagnosis and management of pericardial diseases. Eur Heart J. 2004;25(7):587-610.
Ling LH, Oh JK, Schaff HV, et al. Constrictive pericarditis in the modern era: evolving clinical spectrum and impact on outcome after pericardiectomy. Circulation. 1999;100(13):1380-1386.
Talreja DR, Nishimura RA, Oh JK, Holmes DR Jr. Constrictive pericarditis in the 21st century. Circulation. 2008;117(21):2709-2719.
